prediction.likelyOutcome: Boggess will recover the fair market value of the land taken plus statutory interest regardless of outcome, but its severance-damage claim is in serious trouble: the district court has ruled all three project benefits are 'special' and thus offsettable, UDOT's expert puts that offset at $2.2M, and the jury will now hear that the supposedly impaired remainder was sold in 2016 and developed into two car dealerships. The realistic upside is a partial win narrowing the offset — particularly on the interchange/area-traffic benefit, which looks general under Hempstead — rather than a clean severance award.

issues.label: General vs. Special Benefits Offset (the $2.2M Question)
Value of the Land Physically Taken

outcome.description: On retrial the jury awarded Boggess approximately $330,000 (the opinion gives only this rounded figure) for the value of the condemned property and found no severance damages, after UDOT's expert was allowed to testify to a $2.2 million project-benefit offset. The Court of Appeals held that interstate access and added travel lanes are general benefits that cannot offset severance damages, found the error harmful, reversed the verdict and remanded for a new trial; no fees are discussed.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed for a new trial; no final figure yet.
